7ae89b4162: Four steps to setting lyrics to music
855c9e6265: Start from a motif, a set of chords or a backing, finish the melody first, then write the words. The melody is free, but when you add words later, watch the characters' tones.
4292269841: Write music following the lyrics' sections, syllable counts and emotions. The verse has more words and denser notes; the chorus has fewer words and more long notes, giving the emotion room to stretch.

2c02f69a27: Tone map: the melody follows the rise and fall of the tones
728f47b9d7: The title 〈你是我聽得見卻說不出口的秘密〉 is fourteen characters long. Its last word, 「秘密」, is two 4th tones, so a melody moving from high to low sounds most natural; if the melody rises, it's easily heard as 「迷迷」. Type in your chorus's first line and find the best characters to put high notes on.
bad6656787: The pentatonic scale: drop 4 and 7, and the melody takes on an Eastern colour at once
572058b109: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7: bright and stable, the basis of most pop songs.
80b8a4a61c: 1 2 3 5 6: the pentatonic scale leaves out 4 and 7. Practise short phrases with these five notes first, then try them over chords.
3a97f8102e: 1 ♭3 4 ♯4 5 ♭7: lazy and tense, common in R&B and rock.
167ce4aa64: Steps are smooth; leaps have tension
6a2cad6034: Moving one neighbouring note at a time, such as 1 2 3 2 1. Smooth and speech-like, good for telling the story in the verse.
f1a2e2fbee: A big move of a third or more, such as 1 5 1̇. Creates surprise and an outburst of emotion, good for the start of a chorus.
262fa0d6cf: After a leap, a melody often steps back the other way to fill the gap. Listen to the chorus of 〈我願意〉 and notice how the melody of 「我願意為你」 pushes upward again and again.
94b4c76aef: The emotion rises gradually; common in the pre-chorus
8a876b9017: Letting go, sighing; common at the end of a phrase
ca232f5aa8: Rises then falls, the most complete kind of sentence
b271c10900: Rises and falls within a small range, good for storytelling in the verse
5f4cca1194: Verse and chorus melodies need contrast: the verse sits in the low-to-middle range and moves in waves; the chorus moves higher and opens with an arch or a leap. The clearer the contrast, the more the chorus feels like a release.
